feedback.problem:
Use the definition of Laplace transforms to calculate $F(s)=L{f(t)},$ where $f(t)=u(t-7)$ and $u$ is the unit step function.

$F(s)=L{f(t)}=$
{{field-1}},
valid for $s\,$
{{field-2}}{{field-3}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
We apply the definition of the Laplace transform:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{f(t)} & =F(s)={\int }_{0}^{\infty }f(t){e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the unit step function is defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t)={\begin{aligned}0,\, & t<0 \\ 1,\, & t\ge 0.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

So, for the piecewise function 

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t-7)={\begin{aligned}0,\, & t<7 \\ 1,\, & t\ge 7\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F(s) & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }u(t-7){e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{7}0\cdot {e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{7}^{\infty }1\cdot {e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{7}^{\infty }{e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that this improper integral diverges if $s\le 0.$

For $s>0,$ we calculate this integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}F(s) & ={\int }_{7}^{\infty }{e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{7}^{a}{e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={lim}_{a\to \infty }{(-\frac{{e}^{-st}}{s})|}_{7}^{a} \\  & =-\frac{1}{s}\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }({e}^{-sa}-{e}^{-7s}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{s}(0-{e}^{-7s}) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{-7s}}{s}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Laplace transform of $f(t)$ is

$$
L{f(t)}=\frac{{e}^{-7s}}{s},\,s>0.
$$
